consensus_summary: Darkness primarily symbolizes evil, sin, spiritual blindness/ignorance, and separation from God as the antithesis of light, with common secondary senses of judgment, death/Sheol, primordial chaos, and (more minority) divine mystery or suffering.
book_summary: Concealed disobedience—deeds hidden from the light (opposite: Light).
consensus_core_identification: moral-spiritual evil/sin and separation from God opposed to light
book_core_identification: concealed disobedience (evil deeds hidden from the light)
boundary_disagreement: Book restricts the symbol to the concealment/hiding of disobedient deeds (the John 3:19-20 motif), excluding or sidelining the broader consensus cases of general evil, judgment/outer darkness, death, chaos, divine hiddenness, and affliction.
material_contradiction: None; the book's sense is already an acknowledged facet inside the consensus primary meaning rather than a replacement of it.
rationale: Consensus core is the broad light/dark dualism of evil versus God. Book keeps that same referent category and the opposition to light but materially narrows extension and precision to ‘concealed disobedience,’ treating darkness essentially as the hiding-place of evil deeds. This is boundary refinement, not core replacement or novelty.
strongest_objection: The glossary entry collapses a widely polyvalent biblical symbol into one narrow Johannine aspect, under-representing the dominant broader usage attested across the consensus.
